# dployr

dployr is a deployment platform with a hosted control plane and a lightweight daemon that runs on your own servers. You install dployrd on any VPS or Linux machine, and dployr.io handles the rest: deploy apps, manage services, and monitor servers from the CLI, GitHub Actions, or the web dashboard. No SSH required.

## What it does

- Deploy Node.js, Python, Go, PHP, Java, Ruby, and Docker apps to your own server
- Manage multiple servers from one control plane
- Real-time logs, browser console, rollbacks, environment variables, and secrets
- Blueprints: reusable JSON/YAML/TOML deployment definitions
- Custom domains with automatic SSL (auto-renewed)
- GitHub Actions integration via DPLOYR_TOKEN secret

## How it works

dployrd runs on your server and maintains a persistent mTLS WebSocket connection to Base (the control plane). When you trigger a deployment, Base routes the instruction to the right server. dployrd pulls the code, runs your build steps, and starts the service. No inbound ports, no SSH tunnels.

## Pricing

- Hobby: free forever, 512MB RAM, 1 vCPU, 10GB disk, 1 workload
- Indie: $12/month (annual), 1GB RAM, 1 vCPU, 25GB disk, up to 5 workloads
- Pro: $20/month (annual), 2GB RAM, 1 vCPU, 50GB disk, up to 25 workloads, dedicated instance

## Key concepts

- **Workload**: one running service (API, worker, cron job, etc.)
- **Blueprint**: a declarative deployment config (runtime, source, build steps, env vars)
- **dployrd**: the daemon that runs on your server
- **Base**: the dployr control plane at dployr.io

## Common Questions

**Do I need Docker?** No. Pick a runtime directly. Docker is supported as one option, not a requirement.
**Will traffic spikes raise my bill?** No. You pay for the server, not for what it handles.
**What if a deploy fails?** Your current version stays live until the new one is healthy. Roll back in one click if needed.
**Custom domains and HTTPS?** Yes. Point your domain and SSL is set up and auto-renewed.
**How is this different from Render or Railway?** Render charges per service, Railway charges per usage. dployr charges per server. Run as many workloads as your plan allows at a flat rate.
